listing.name: Crackdown (Crackdown Recompiled)
listing.summary: Add a prepared Crackdown copy from the Windows package or Linux AppImage, preserving its exact original-data requirements, upstream-owned updates and separate base/TU6 save generations.

steps.title: Finish exact original-disc setup upstream
steps.instruction: Use the complete Windows package or Linux AppImage and your own original, unupdated Crackdown Xbox360 retail disc: title4D5307DC, Default.xex14,270,464bytes, SHA-256 7AAA7A8920D1C3C737E58CF583DEBAFE6013BE0A96BEC3EC136E5DE7E3377E5A. Complete upstream ISO/extracted-folder validation and installation until Ready to play; game/ is adjacent and $SystemUpdate is unnecessary. No disc extraction, original acquisition, compilation or installer is invoked by this registration.

steps.title: Select the prepared native game entry
steps.instruction: Select crackdown.exe, its complete containing writable package directory and no arguments for ordinary Play. Keep the matching SDK/runtime/GPU DLLs, launcher resources, game data, configuration and notices together. The embedded launcher calls the native ReXApp game path in-process. Review and consent to the exact executable/CWD/arguments, then request Play separately. Windows10/11 x64, Direct3D12 and the applicable VC++ x64 runtime remain upstream prerequisites. On Linux, select the CrackdownRecompiled AppImage itself, with its folder as the working folder and no arguments; it needs no Windows runtime.

steps.title: Complete restarts and updates outside attachment
steps.instruction: Window size, monitor, VSync or adapter changes can make the next launcher Play start a successor window/process; upstream restart explicitly relaunches and quits the selected process. Finish settings/setup/restart and upstream updater work separately, close every actual game/helper/successor, then attach the resulting prepared player. Do not register trg-updater.exe or rely on automatic successor adoption/termination. Upstream/user is the sole runtime-replacement owner; Core offers no external update or rollback.

steps.title: Retain upstream save switching and cleanup boundaries
steps.instruction: Normal startup selects base or the separately installed TU6 guest and can recover an interrupted save switch, snapshot/swap live profile and campaign/header slots, then remove completed .switch-* staging under save-versions. These are upstream-owned writes, not Portcove migration or cross-version compatibility promises. TU6 and Four-Play/Free-for-All DLC are optional separately owned inputs with their own exact source checks; Free-for-All requires TU6. Do not remove/update content through this guide. The updater constructor may remove %TEMP%/trg-update-* directories older than24hours; ordinary exit may remove non-crash session logs unless detailed logging is enabled. Preserve recovery/diagnostic copies separately before startup/maintenance.

steps.title: Manage this copy yourself
steps.instruction: Removing registration preserves external files; no external backup/restore, deletion, save conversion or managed maintenance is offered.

warnings: This guide’s source evidence is for v0.6.2; later source revisions differ. The published package SHA-256 is the provider’s expected value. Portcove has not inspected the ZIP or executable files or confirmed which source and SDK produced them.

Keep a separate complete recovery copy outside upstream transaction/workspace directories.

references.title: Back up the actual user-data root before first prepared startup
references.instruction: The selected source uses user_data/ beside the program, or explicit --user_data_root; if the default is not writable it refuses rather than claiming another profile. Preserve settings.toml, all4D5307DC profile/campaign/header data, save-versions/base and tu6 snapshots, achievements, caches, separate originals/game/, logs and every actual --cache_root/--update_data_root/custom location. No legacy Documents migration is inferred from another title. Keep a separate complete recovery copy outside upstream transaction/workspace directories.
